intent.raw_query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June 2026 from Chicago

experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of art history.

experiences.name: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere sampling local Roman street food including supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, and pair them with local Frascati wine at family-run trattorias and wine bars frequented by locals.

experiences.name: Borghese Gallery Art Tour
experiences.description: Visit this intimate yet world-class gallery housing Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings inside a beautiful villa. Reservations are mandatory and entry is limited, making it an exclusive and immersive art experience unlike any other in Rome.

experiences.name: Testaccio Market & Cooking Class
experiences.description: Start your morning at Rome's most authentic food market, Mercato Testaccio, where locals shop for fresh produce, cheese, and cured meats. Follow it with a hands-on pasta and tiramisu cooking class led by a local chef using ingredients sourced directly from the market.

experiences.name: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Exploration
experiences.description: Walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire across the Roman Forum and up to Palatine Hill, where emperors once lived. The combined ticket also includes the Colosseum, offering an unparalleled journey through ancient Roman art, architecture, and civilization.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use the time to rest on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome Fiumicino Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Leonardo Express train (€14) or the cheaper FL1 regional train (€8) to Roma Termini. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a relaxed evening stroll to the nearby neighborhood to get oriented — explore the local streets, find a nearby alimentari (grocery store) for snacks and water supplies to save money throughout the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Trastevere neighborhood (reachable by tram or bus) for a classic Roman evening atmosphere. Wander the cobblestone streets, admire the Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free entry), and soak in the lively piazza atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or grab a quick cornetto (croissant) and cappuccino at a bar near Roma Termini for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick suppli (fried rice ball) or pizza al taglio (pizza by the slice) near the hotel for €3–5 from a local rosticceria.
meals.dinner: Trattoria da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — a beloved local trattoria with authentic Roman dishes like cacio e pepe and coda alla vaccinara. Budget around €15–20 per person including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 48-hour or 72-hour public transport pass (€7 or €12) at Roma Termini to save on bus and tram fares throughout the trip. Stock up on bottled water and snacks at a supermarket (Conad or MD) near the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Start early at the Colosseum and Roman Forum. Book tickets online in advance (€16 combined ticket) to skip the lines. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the ancient amphitheater and walking through the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, all included in the same ticket. Arrive by 8:30 AM to beat the crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 15 minutes to Circus Maximus (free, outdoor) and then stroll through the Aventine Hill neighborhood. Visit the famous Keyhole of the Knights of Malta on Aventine Hill — a perfectly framed free view of St. Peter's Basilica dome. Then walk to the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) for panoramic views of Rome — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Testaccio neighborhood, Rome's traditional working-class food district. Browse the Testaccio Market (closes around 2 PM on weekdays, so plan accordingly) or simply explore the streets. End the evening with a gelato from a local gelateria.

meals.breakfast: Bar/café near the hotel — espresso and cornetto for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina or a nearby pizza al taglio spot near the Forum area — budget €5–8 for a satisfying slice and drink.
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — famous for traditional Roman cuisine like rigatoni alla pajata and abbacchio. Budget €15–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Day 2 involves significant walking on uneven ancient cobblestones. Bring a reusable water bottle; Rome has free drinking fountains called 'nasoni' throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel — book tickets online well in advance (€17 standard entry) to avoid long queues. Spend 2–3 hours marveling at the world's greatest art collection, including Raphael's Rooms and Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican Museums, walk directly into St. Peter's Basilica (free entry — no ticket needed). Climb to the top of St. Peter's Dome for panoramic views of Rome (€8 with stairs, €10 with elevator). Explore St. Peter's Square and the surrounding Borgo neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Tiber River toward Castel Sant'Angelo (exterior is free to admire; entry is €14 if you wish to go inside — skip to save budget). Continue to the lively Prati neighborhood for dinner and a peaceful evening walk.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a pastry and coffee at a local bar near the hotel — €2–3.
meals.lunch: Forno Roscioli or a nearby bakery near the Vatican — grab focaccia, pizza bianca, or a panino for €4–6.
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati — a beloved neighborhood trattoria offering a fixed-price Roman menu (cacio e pepe, saltimbocca) for around €15–18 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Dress code is strictly enforced at the Vatican — no bare shoulders or knees. Bring a scarf or light layer. The Vatican Museums are extremely crowded; arrive right at opening time (9:00 AM) for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic centro storico (historic center). Visit the Pantheon (€5 entry — one of the world's best-preserved ancient buildings), then walk to the nearby Piazza Navona (free) with its stunning Baroque fountains by Bernini. Browse the street artists and performers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the Campo de' Fiori market (free to browse, closes around 2 PM) — a lively open-air market perfect for picking up fresh fruit, local cheeses, and cured meats for a budget picnic lunch. Afterward, visit the beautiful Largo di Torre Argentina (free outdoor archaeological site where Julius Caesar was assassinated).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Trevi Fountain at dusk (free) — less crowded than midday. Toss a coin for good luck, then walk to the Spanish Steps (free) for a classic Roman evening. Explore the elegant Via Condotti and Via del Corso for window shopping.

meals.breakfast: Local bar near the hotel — espresso and cornetto for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Self-assembled picnic from Campo de' Fiori market — fresh bread, cheese, salumi, and fruit for €6–8 per person. Eat in Piazza Navona or a nearby park.
meals.dinner: Osteria Barberini near the Trevi Fountain area — cozy neighborhood restaurant with pasta dishes for €10–14 per person. Alternatively, grab a hearty suppli and pizza al taglio from Supplì Roma for €6–8.

day_by_day.notes: The Pantheon is best visited early morning to avoid crowds. Many churches in Rome's centro storico (Sant'Ignazio, San Luigi dei Francesi with Caravaggio paintings) offer free entry and world-class art — don't miss them!

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery — one of Rome's finest art museums housing masterpieces by Bernini, Caravaggio, and Raphael. Entry is €13 but reservations are mandatory (book weeks in advance — timed entry slots fill up fast). Spend 2 hours in this intimate, world-class gallery.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, explore the surrounding Villa Borghese park (free) — Rome's version of Central Park. Rent a rowboat on the lake (€5–6 per person for 20 minutes) or simply relax on the grass. Walk or take a bus to the Piazza del Popolo (free) with its twin churches and Egyptian obelisk, and climb the nearby Pincian Hill terrace for a sweeping panoramic view of Rome.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Flaminio and Prati neighborhoods. Visit the MAXXI (National Museum of 21st Century Arts) exterior — a stunning Zaha Hadid-designed building — or enter for €12 if the current exhibition interests you. Stroll along the Tiber at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Bar near the hotel — espresso and pastry for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese park — pick up supplies from a nearby alimentari or enjoy a quick panino from a local bar for €4–6.
meals.dinner: Pizzarium Bonci (Via della Meloria) in Prati — considered Rome's best pizza al taglio by legendary baker Gabriele Bonci. Budget €8–12 for a generous and extraordinary meal.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets MUST be booked in advance — this is non-negotiable. The gallery limits visitors to 360 per two-hour slot. Book at borghese.it as soon as possible.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning bus or metro to the Ostiense neighborhood to visit the Pyramid of Cestius (exterior free) and the beautiful Non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico — €3 suggested donation), where Keats and Shelley are buried. Then explore the vibrant street art scene in the Ostiense/Pigneto area — one of Rome's most creative neighborhoods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Capitoline Museums (€15) — the world's oldest public museums, housing incredible Roman sculptures, the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, and stunning views of the Roman Forum from the terrace. Alternatively, explore the Aventine and Garbatella neighborhoods on foot for a more local, off-the-beaten-path experience (free).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere for a final evening in one of Rome's most atmospheric neighborhoods. Browse the Saturday evening market stalls, listen to street musicians in the piazza, and enjoy a leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: Try a local bar in the Ostiense area for a true neighborhood experience — espresso and cornetto for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Mercato Testaccio (open Saturday mornings) — grab street food like supplì, fried artichokes, and fresh pasta for €6–10.
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 or Tonnarello in Trastevere — both offer authentic Roman pasta and secondi for €14–18 per person. Arrive early (7:00–7:30 PM) to avoid long waits on Saturday evenings.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is a great day to experience Rome's neighborhood markets. The Porta Portese flea market (Sunday morning) is worth planning around if you extend your stay. Wear comfortable shoes for the Capitoline Museums — lots of stairs and marble floors.

day_by_day.morning: Take advantage of the first Sunday of the month (if applicable) when many state museums offer free entry — including the Colosseum, Borghese Gallery, and national museums. Even on a regular Sunday, explore the Porta Portese Flea Market (7:00 AM – 2:00 PM, free to browse) in Trastevere — Rome's largest and most famous flea market, perfect for unique souvenirs on a budget.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the beautiful Basilica di San Giovanni in Laterano (free) — Rome's cathedral and one of the most important churches in Christianity, often overlooked by tourists. Nearby, see the Scala Santa (Holy Stairs) and the ancient Baptistery. Walk through the Celio neighborhood and visit the Basilica dei Santi Quattro Coronati (free) for a peaceful, crowd-free art experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Rome — return to your favorite neighborhood for a farewell dinner. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Spend any remaining budget on local food souvenirs: artisanal pasta, local olive oil, or Roman cookies from a nearby alimentari.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer breakfast at a historic café — try a maritozzo (Roman cream-filled bun) and cappuccino for €4–5.
meals.lunch: Grab a final pizza al taglio or a warm suppli from a rosticceria near the hotel — €5–7.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a neighborhood trattoria of your choice — splurge slightly on a full Roman meal: antipasto, pasta, secondo, and house wine for €20–25 per person as a final treat.

day_by_day.notes: Check departure flight time and plan accordingly. The Leonardo Express from Roma Termini to Fiumicino runs every 30 minutes and takes 32 minutes (€14). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Keep €14–20 in cash for the airport train.

trip_options.title: Classic Rome Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of art history.

experiences.description: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere sampling local Roman street food including supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, and pair them with local Frascati wine at family-run trattorias and wine bars frequented by locals.

experiences.name: Borghese Gallery Art Tour
experiences.description: Visit this intimate yet world-class gallery housing Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings inside a beautiful villa. Reservations are mandatory and entry is limited, making it an exclusive and immersive art experience unlike any other in Rome.

experiences.name: Testaccio Market & Cooking Class
experiences.description: Start your morning at Rome's most authentic food market, Mercato Testaccio, where locals shop for fresh produce, cheese, and cured meats. Follow it with a hands-on pasta and tiramisu cooking class led by a local chef using ingredients sourced directly from the market.

experiences.name: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Exploration
experiences.description: Walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire across the Roman Forum and up to Palatine Hill, where emperors once lived. The combined ticket also includes the Colosseum, offering an unparalleled journey through ancient Roman art, architecture, and civilization.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Rome airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take the Leonardo Express train or a pre-booked shuttle to your hotel (Aegean Bliss Resort, Rome). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through your neighborhood to get your bearings. Stop at a local alimentari (deli) to pick up snacks and water.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Rome with a gentle evening walk along the Tiber River. Head to the Trastevere neighborhood for your first authentic Roman dinner — explore the charming cobblestone lanes and soak in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or grab a quick espresso and cornetto at the airport café upon landing.
meals.lunch: Light snack at the airport or on the train — pick up a tramezzino (Italian sandwich) from a station bar.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Trattoria Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — a beloved mid-range Roman trattoria famous for cacio e pepe, coda alla vaccinara, and seasonal vegetables. Budget approx. €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Avoid booking any timed-entry experiences on arrival day. Purchase a 48-hour or 72-hour transit card at the airport for easy metro and bus access throughout your stay.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel: Begin your day early with a pre-booked skip-the-line entry to the Vatican Museums. Spend 3–4 hours exploring one of the world's greatest art collections — ancient sculptures, Renaissance tapestries, the Gallery of Maps, and finally Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book the first entry slot (8:00 AM) to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross St. Peter's Square and visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry). Climb the dome for panoramic views over Rome if energy permits (€8). Afterward, walk across the Ponte Sant'Angelo to the Castel Sant'Angelo for exterior photos and a riverside coffee break.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rest during the hottest part of the late afternoon, then head out for an evening aperitivo. Visit a local enoteca near your hotel for a Spritz or Negroni with complimentary cicchetti before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at a nearby bar — espresso, cappuccino, and a fresh cornetto. Budget €3–6.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Vatican at Pizzarium Bonci (Via della Meloria) — Rome's most celebrated pizza al taglio spot. Try the seasonal toppings. Budget €10–15.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Il Sorpasso in Prati neighborhood — a stylish yet affordable wine bar and restaurant with excellent Roman dishes and a great wine list. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets MUST be booked in advance online (museivaticani.va). Morning slots sell out weeks ahead, especially in June. Dress code required: no bare shoulders or shorts above the knee inside the Vatican.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour: Take a taxi or bus to the Villa Borghese park for your timed-entry visit to the Borghese Gallery (entry is strictly by reservation, 2-hour slots). Marvel at Bernini's extraordinary sculptures — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — alongside Caravaggio's dramatic paintings in an intimate, world-class setting. This is one of Rome's most rewarding art experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens. Rent a rowboat on the small lake (€3–5) or simply relax in the shade. Walk down the Spanish Steps (Scalinata di Trinità dei Monti) and explore the upscale Via Condotti area and the charming streets around Piazza del Popolo.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the historic center for the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere sampling local Roman street food including supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, bruschetta, and local wines at family-run bars and street vendors.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café near your hotel — cappuccino and a pastry. Budget €4–6.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — pick up fresh bread, cheese, cured meats, and fruit from a nearby alimentari or Mercato Trionfale. Budget €10–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner included as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk experience, or supplement with a sit-down meal at Osteria della Gensola — a mid-range Roman-Sicilian restaurant with excellent seafood pasta. Budget €30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets are mandatory and must be reserved well in advance at galleriaborghese.it — only 360 visitors are admitted per 2-hour slot. Arrive 15 minutes early or you may lose your spot.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Cooking Class: Start your morning at Rome's most authentic food market, Mercato Testaccio, where locals shop for fresh produce, cheese, cured meats, and Roman street food. Join a guided cooking class that begins with a market tour — learn to select seasonal ingredients, then head to a nearby kitchen to prepare classic Roman dishes such as cacio e pepe, supplì, and tiramisu.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class (and eating your creations for lunch!), walk off the meal by exploring the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's traditional working-class district. Visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico) where Keats and Shelley are buried, and admire the ancient Pyramid of Cestius nearby. Browse the vintage and artisan shops along Via Marmorata.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Tiber to the vibrant Pigneto or Ostiense neighborhood for a relaxed evening. Explore street art, enjoy a craft beer at a local bar, and have a casual dinner at a neighborhood trattoria.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the market — espresso and a pastry at a local bar in Testaccio. Budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes prepared during the cooking class — typically included in the experience cost.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — a legendary, affordable trattoria built into the Monte dei Cocci (ancient pottery shard hill), serving outstanding Roman classics. Budget €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market & Cooking Class experience typically runs from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM. Book in advance through Airbnb Experiences or local operators like Eating Italy Food Tours. Wear comfortable shoes for the market walk.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Exploration: Head to the ancient heart of Rome early in the morning to beat the heat and crowds. Walk through the Roman Forum — the center of political and civic life in ancient Rome — and climb up to Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the Colosseum, Circus Maximus, and the city skyline. Allow 3–4 hours to fully explore both sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Forum, walk to the iconic Colosseum for exterior photos (or purchase a combined ticket for interior access — book online in advance). Then take a break in the shade at a nearby café. In the late afternoon, wander through the Celio neighborhood and visit the beautiful Basilica di San Clemente — a multi-layered church descending from the 12th century to ancient Roman times below street level (€10 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in the Monti neighborhood — Rome's hippest historic district. Browse independent boutiques, aperitivo bars, and street art before settling in for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a café near the hotel. Budget €4–7.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a trattoria near the Colosseum — try Ristorante Aroma for a splurge with Colosseum views, or opt for a more budget-friendly panino from a nearby alimentari. Mid-range option: €15–25.
meals.dinner: Dinner in the Monti neighborhood at Urbana 47 — a charming farm-to-table restaurant using local and seasonal ingredients, with a warm, relaxed atmosphere. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a combined Colosseum + Roman Forum + Palatine Hill ticket online at coopculture.it well in advance — timed entry is required and tickets sell out fast in June. Bring a refillable water bottle; Rome's free drinking fountains (nasoni) are everywhere and the water is excellent.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Rome's lesser-visited art churches — begin at Santa Maria Maggiore (one of Rome's four major basilicas, free entry), then walk to San Luigi dei Francesi to see Caravaggio's stunning St. Matthew cycle of paintings (free, small donation expected). Continue to Sant'Agostino to see another Caravaggio. This self-guided art church walk is one of Rome's best-kept secrets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at and around the Pantheon (free entry with Roma Pass or small fee) — one of the world's best-preserved ancient buildings. Then wander through the lively Piazza Navona, admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, and explore the antique shops and galleries along Via dei Coronari. Stop for a gelato at one of the area's artisan gelaterie.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a memorable final full-evening dinner experience. Head to Campo de' Fiori for a pre-dinner Aperol Spritz at a terrace bar, then walk to a nearby restaurant for a special Roman meal.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café near your hotel. Try a maritozzo (cream-filled sweet bun) — a classic Roman breakfast treat. Budget €4–6.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Osteria dell'Ingegno near the Pantheon — a reliable mid-range spot with Roman pasta, seasonal antipasti, and good house wine. Budget €20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Roscioli Ristorante Salumeria — a legendary Roman institution combining a world-class deli, wine cellar, and restaurant. Excellent cacio e pepe, carbonara, and charcuterie. Book in advance. Budget €35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The best gelato near the Pantheon is at Giolitti or Della Palma — avoid any gelateria with gelato piled high in mountains (a sign of artificial ingredients). Look for gelato stored in covered metal containers — that's the artisan sign of quality.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — take a slow, unhurried walk through whichever neighborhood you loved most. Visit any last-minute spots you may have missed: toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain (arrive early morning for smaller crowds), browse the Sunday market at Porta Portese (if it's a Sunday), or revisit a favorite café for one last perfect espresso.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and store your luggage at the concierge if your flight is later. Spend your final afternoon doing light souvenir shopping — pick up quality Italian products like olive oil, pasta, wine, or artisan ceramics from reputable shops rather than tourist traps. Via della Croce and the streets around Campo de' Fiori have excellent food shops.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport for your departure flight. Enjoy a final espresso at the airport and reflect on an unforgettable week in Rome.

meals.breakfast: Final Roman breakfast at your favorite café — savor a perfectly made cappuccino and fresh cornetto one last time. Budget €4–6.
meals.lunch: Casual farewell lunch at a trattoria or wine bar near the hotel. Try supplì al telefono (fried rice balls with mozzarella) and a glass of Frascati white wine — a perfect Roman goodbye. Budget €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the airport or on the flight, depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in, especially from central Rome. The Leonardo Express from Roma Termini to Fiumicino Airport runs every 30 minutes and takes 32 minutes (€14). If departing from Ciampino airport, allow extra time as it requires a bus connection.

Visit a nearby enoteca for a curated aperitivo tasting of local Lazio wines and artisanal cheeses — a gentle, low-commitment introduction to Roman culture after a long flight.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — Join an exclusive small-group or private evening tour through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere, sampling supplì, cacio e pepe bites, artisan gelato, and paired local wines. meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast on the plane or a light snack at the airport lounge before departure.
meals.lunch: Upon arrival, indulge in a welcome lunch at the hotel's signature restaurant — expect fresh Roman antipasti, house-made pasta, and a glass of chilled Frascati.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Paris (Trastevere) — A celebrated fine-dining institution serving elevated Roman classics like coda alla vaccinara and artichoke alla giudia in an elegant 19th-century setting.

day_by_day.evening: Castel Sant'Angelo Sunset Visit — Take a private guided tour of Castel Sant'Angelo at golden hour for stunning views of the Tiber River and the Rome skyline. This former papal fortress offers a dramatic and romantic setting as the city lights begin to shimmer.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — Enjoy a lavish spread at the Aegean Bliss Resort's restaurant, with freshly baked cornetti, seasonal fruit, eggs, and premium Italian cold cuts.
meals.lunch: Il Sorpasso (Prati) — A beloved modern Roman bistro near the Vatican offering exceptional cicchetti, charcuterie boards, and natural wines in a stylish setting.
meals.dinner: Settimio all'Arancio — An intimate, refined trattoria near the Vatican known for its seasonal Roman cuisine, house-made pasta, and outstanding wine cellar. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums early-access tickets months in advance — demand is extremely high in June. Consider a private guide for the full Vatican experience. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for cobblestone streets and the dome climb.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour — Visit this world-class intimate gallery housing Bernini's extraordinary sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic masterpieces. Entry is strictly timed and limited, making it feel exclusive by design. A private art historian guide will enrich the experience with context and storytelling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Gardens & Pincian Hill Stroll — After the gallery, spend a relaxed afternoon walking through the manicured Villa Borghese gardens. Rent a rowboat on the ornamental lake or hire a private electric golf cart tour of the grounds. Stroll to the Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping panoramic views over Piazza del Popolo and Rome's rooftops.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo & Elegant Dinner in Parioli — Head to Rome's upscale Parioli neighborhood for a sophisticated aperitivo at a chic rooftop bar, followed by dinner at one of Rome's finest contemporary restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Café Sant'Eustachio — Rome's most legendary espresso bar, serving coffee roasted in-house since 1938. Pair with a fresh cornetto alla crema for an authentic Roman breakfast ritual.
meals.lunch: Caffè delle Arti (inside Villa Borghese) — A beautifully located café-restaurant within the gallery complex offering Mediterranean cuisine in a refined garden setting.
meals.dinner: Il Pagliaccio (2 Michelin Stars) — One of Rome's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurants, offering a creative and seasonal tasting menu that masterfully blends Italian tradition with avant-garde technique. Advance reservation essential.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery strictly limits entry to 360 visitors per 2-hour slot — pre-booking is mandatory and should be arranged weeks ahead. The gallery is closed on Mondays. June weather in Rome can be warm (25–32°C), so light, breathable clothing is recommended for outdoor afternoon activities.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Cooking Class — Immerse yourself in authentic Roman food culture with a private morning experience at Mercato Testaccio, Rome's most beloved local market. Shop alongside your chef-instructor for seasonal ingredients — fresh pasta, aged pecorino, local produce, and cured meats — then head to a premium cooking studio for a hands-on class preparing a traditional Roman feast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Exploration — After lunch, embark on a private guided tour of the ancient heart of the Roman Empire. Walk the Roman Forum's sacred road, explore the ruins of temples and basilicas, then ascend Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the Colosseum and Circus Maximus. Your expert guide will bring 2,000 years of history vividly to life.
day_by_day.evening: Colosseum by Night (Private Access) — Experience the iconic Colosseum under the stars with a rare private after-hours access tour. With the crowds gone and the monument dramatically lit, this is an utterly unforgettable Roman experience available exclusively to premium guests.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at the Aegean Bliss Resort — take your time with a full spread before the market visit.
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you personally prepared during the cooking class — a private dining experience in the cooking studio, paired with Lazio wines selected by your instructor.
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) — A legendary Roman trattoria embedded into the ancient Monte dei Cocci hill, serving exceptional traditional Roman cuisine including rigatoni alla pajata and abbacchio. Rustic yet refined.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio neighborhood is the historic culinary heart of Rome — locals consider it the most authentic district in the city. Colosseum night tours must be arranged through licensed private tour operators well in advance as availability is very limited. Wear comfortable shoes for extensive walking on uneven ancient stones.

day_by_day.morning: Capitoline Museums Private Tour — Explore the world's oldest public museums, perched dramatically atop Capitoline Hill. View the original bronze equestrian statue of Marcus Aurelius, the iconic Capitoline Wolf, and breathtaking views over the Roman Forum from the museum terraces. A private guide will contextualize Rome's artistic and political legacy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pantheon, Navona & Campo de' Fiori Discovery Walk — With a private guide, visit the perfectly preserved Pantheon (a marvel of ancient engineering), stroll through the baroque splendor of Piazza Navona with its Bernini fountains, and explore the vibrant Campo de' Fiori market square. Browse high-end antique dealers and artisan boutiques along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop Aperitivo & Gourmet Dinner near the Historic Centre — Ascend to one of Rome's finest rooftop terraces for a sunset Negroni and panoramic views, then settle into an intimate fine-dining experience in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Roscioli Caffè Pasticceria — A celebrated Roman institution near Campo de' Fiori known for exceptional espresso, freshly baked pastries, and artisan breakfast selections beloved by locals and connoisseurs alike.
meals.lunch: Ristorante Fortunato al Pantheon — A classic, elegant Roman restaurant steps from the Pantheon, serving refined traditional dishes to politicians, artists, and discerning travelers since 1975.
meals.dinner: La Pergola (3 Michelin Stars) — Rome's only three-Michelin-star restaurant, perched atop the Rome Cavalieri hotel with sweeping panoramic views of the Eternal City. Chef Heinz Beck's legendary Mediterranean cuisine is a once-in-a-lifetime dining experience. Reserve months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola is the crown jewel of Rome's fine dining scene — a jacket is required for gentlemen and the dress code is strictly elegant. The wine cellar holds over 60,000 labels. This is the ideal evening for a special celebration if applicable. Book a private car for the evening to ensure seamless transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Palazzo Doria Pamphilj Private Art Visit — Discover one of Rome's best-kept secrets: a magnificent privately owned baroque palace still inhabited by the Doria Pamphilj family, housing a stunning collection of Velázquez, Caravaggio, Titian, and Raphael works. Arrange a private family-guided tour for an extraordinarily intimate and exclusive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury Shopping & Artisan Ateliers — Dedicate the afternoon to Rome's finest shopping streets. Explore Via Condotti for international luxury houses (Bulgari, Valentino, Fendi), then venture into the artisan quarter near Via del Governo Vecchio for bespoke leather goods, custom tailoring, and rare antiquarian bookshops. End with a private appointment at a renowned Roman goldsmith or ceramics atelier.
day_by_day.evening: Private Sunset Boat Tour on the Tiber — Board a private luxury boat for a curated sunset cruise along the Tiber River, gliding past illuminated landmarks including Castel Sant'Angelo, the ancient bridges, and riverside palaces. Champagne and canapés are served on board as the city glows in the evening light.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — enjoy a leisurely spread at the resort before heading out for the day's cultural immersion.
meals.lunch: Antico Arco (Gianicolo Hill) — A refined and creative Roman restaurant on the Gianicolo hill with a seasonal menu, exceptional wine list, and a beautiful garden terrace perfect for a long Saturday lunch.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Pipero Roma — A sophisticated, Michelin-starred dining room in the heart of Rome offering inventive contemporary Italian cuisine with impeccable service and an extraordinary natural wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: The Palazzo Doria Pamphilj private family tour must be arranged directly with the palace administration — it is rarely advertised and represents a truly exclusive cultural privilege. The Tiber boat tour should be pre-booked through a luxury concierge service. June evenings are warm and perfect for outdoor experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Appian Way Private Cycling or Carriage Tour — Escape the city on the ancient Via Appia Antica, Rome's oldest road, lined with pine trees, ancient tombs, catacombs, and pastoral countryside. Explore by private vintage bicycle or horse-drawn carriage for an utterly romantic and cinematic experience. Visit the Catacombs of San Callisto with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Thermal Spa & Farewell Relaxation — Return to the Aegean Bliss Resort for a luxurious afternoon at the hotel spa. Indulge in a signature treatment — a warm stone massage, a Roman-inspired thermal ritual, or a personalized wellness journey — as a restorative farewell to Rome. Pack at leisure and savor the final hours in your beachfront suite.
day_by_day.evening: Grand Farewell Dinner — Conclude the journey with a spectacular final dinner at one of Rome's most celebrated and atmospheric restaurants, toasting to an unforgettable week in the Eternal City.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel champagne breakfast on your private terrace or balcony — a leisurely, indulgent start to the final day with fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, smoked salmon, and Prosecco.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the Appian Way — arranged by your private guide or concierge, featuring a curated hamper of Roman charcuterie, artisan cheeses, local olives, sourdough bread, and a bottle of chilled Frascati, enjoyed among the ancient ruins.
meals.dinner: Imàgo (Hassler Hotel Rooftop) — Perched atop the Spanish Steps with the most dramatic panoramic views in Rome, Imàgo offers a Michelin-starred contemporary Italian menu in an extraordinarily romantic setting — the perfect farewell to the Eternal City.

day_by_day.notes: If departing the following morning, arrange a private chauffeur transfer to Fiumicino for an early departure. Request a late checkout from the Aegean Bliss Resort if your flight allows. Consider purchasing artisan gifts or gourmet items (aged pecorino, truffle products, local wines) during the week to bring home as souvenirs of your Roman journey.
